PullRequest.Title: sessions: move Customizations next to Automations
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- replace the separate Customizations shortcuts pane with a single Customizations entry next to Automations
- place the Sessions header and its existing New, Filter, and Find actions directly below the navigation entries
- preserve desktop and phone behavior, accessibility, focus handling, and session-row hover styling
- remove the obsolete Customizations toolbar widget, styles, and fixture

## Validation

- `npm run compile`
- `npm run hygiene`
- focused Sessions list, header, and New button tests

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call path and synchronous geometry read are explicit, and the tree implementation confirms full rendered-row disposal/re-render on setChildren without diff options. Exact milliseconds and event prevalence vary by provider and list size, which affects severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: DOM style and layout work across the rendered sessions tree
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost is paid once per SessionsList.update/refresh and the forced layout must resolve the DOM mutations made while re-rendering the currently visible rows; it therefore grows with provider/session change frequency and rendered sidebar complexity.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased synchronous update latency and sidebar jank while sessions are changing
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The Sessions header remained outside the object tree. Its width-dependent layout was measured only from SessionsView layout/find-state paths, so ordinary session-list model updates did not detach, append, and synchronously measure the header.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The header is now a tree row, and every renderElement call appends it and immediately invokes updateHeaderLayout. That callback writes display styles and reads headerLabel.clientWidth, synchronously resolving layout during the tree's root splice.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 495 calls this.layoutHeader() from SessionsHeaderRenderer.renderElement immediately after appending the live header. SessionsList.update still calls tree.setChildren(null, children), whose non-diff object-tree splice disposes and reinserts visible rows on each update, so this new callback runs for each visible-list refresh.
Findings.Title: Keep header measurement out of list refresh rendering
Findings.Impact: With the Sessions sidebar visible, each provider/session update—such as title, status, read, or archive changes during active work—now introduces a synchronous layout flush while the list is rebuilding. This lengthens UI-thread refreshes and can make the sidebar stutter, especially with many visible rows or concurrent session changes.
Findings.Evidence: SessionsList.update ends in tree.setChildren(null, children) (line 4073) and is reached from visible provider onDidChangeSessions refreshes, list-model changes, active-session changes, filters, and other events. ObjectTreeModel.setChildren performs a full splice without diffIdentityProvider; ListView._splice calls disposeElement for rendered rows and then renderElement on reused rows. The new renderer therefore removes/re-appends the header and invokes SessionsView.updateHeaderLayout, whose desktop path reads headerLabel.clientWidth after setting display styles (sessionsView.ts:623-646), forcing layout in the middle of the refresh.
Findings.Recommendation: Do not call the width-measuring updateHeaderLayout from renderElement on every model refresh. Keep it on the existing view resize and find-open/close paths, and if initial reparenting needs a pass, coalesce a single measurement after rendering (for example on the next animation frame) rather than measuring inside the tree splice.

Scenarios.Scenario: Desktop Sessions sidebar initial render and subsequent session-list refreshes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SessionsList.update rebuilds the object-tree children synchronously; visible rows are disposed/re-rendered before the sidebar refresh completes. The new header renderer invokes width-dependent header layout during that splice, so browser layout is on the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronous DOM geometry read (headerLabel.clientWidth) after header/style mutations, forcing browser style/layout resolution
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once for each visible desktop SessionsList.update/refresh while the header row is rendered
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The static header was outside the list and was measured only on view layout or find-state transitions, not on ordinary list model refreshes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks completion of the list refresh on the UI thread and splits DOM mutation work with a synchronous layout flush.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Refresh frequency from provider session changes, list-model changes, active-session changes, and filters; each forced layout resolves mutations for the currently rendered rows, whose count is bounded by the viewport but whose DOM complexity varies.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Updates are synchronous on the UI thread. Active-session changes are frame-scheduled, but provider/list-model refreshes are not coalesced by this change; each update performs its own root splice and header measurement.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The object tree reuses row templates by template ID but does not diff this setChildren call, so template reuse does not avoid disposeElement/renderElement or the header measurement. No cold/warm cache avoids the geometry read.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed renderElement call, downstream clientWidth read, update callers, and non-diff tree splice behavior are explicit in repository code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact refresh rates, rendered-row complexity, and browser layout duration vary by provider and user session count; this limits severity to medium, but not confidence in the mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable regression: the PR adds a synchronous layout measurement to every visible list refresh; the finding recommends keeping measurement on resize/find paths or coalescing it after rendering.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening Customizations from the new navigation row
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A click executes sessions.customization.overview, synchronizes the active harness, obtains the singleton editor input, and awaits editorService.openEditor before showing the welcome page.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open or reveal the AI Customizations management editor
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One editorService.openEditor call per command invocation; singleton input reuse applies on warm opens
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The removed Overview customization shortcut invoked the same openCustomizationOverviewPage logic and one editor open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The click waits for editor opening before selecting the welcome page.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One command execution per user click and one editor input; no loop over sessions or customization items is added.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The editor open is awaited as one operation. Repeated clicks are governed by the singleton editor input/editor service rather than new PR-local fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: AICustomizationManagementEditorInput.getOrCreate reuses the singleton while alive. The PR retains the same active-session descriptor lookup and editor-open path that the prior Overview shortcut used.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the expensive operation is unchanged; the old and new helpers are equivalent.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Downstream editor initialization cost depends on editor state and customization providers, but the diff does not increase its cardinality or move it onto a background/startup path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: navigation is consolidated, but the expensive editor-open operation remains one-for-one with the prior Overview action.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: After restoration, ActiveSessionHarnessSyncContribution observes the active session and available harnesses and updates an in-memory observable. The Sessions list creates lightweight navigation rows; the removed customizations widget is no longer eagerly built.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Available harness count for descriptor lookup and a fixed number of shortcut rows. The prior customization toolbar's multiple model/count observers and DOM controls are removed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable reactions run synchronously when active session or available harnesses change; no new asynchronous burst, limiter, queue, subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network call is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Harness descriptors are held by the existing service; active session writes use the existing observable and unchanged invalidation. No new cache or negative-cache state is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the contribution logic is materially the same as before, while the eager toolbar/widget and count observers are deleted.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The amount of startup work saved depends on enabled customization providers, but there is no evidence of a changed expensive external boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; this path removes eager UI/model observation rather than adding it. Evidence does not establish a shipped performance symptom strongly enough to record a regression fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Phone/desktop layout transitions and sidebar resizing
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A context-key transition rebuilds the list and moves the Sessions header between its static phone container and desktop tree row; resize runs SplitView layout, then SessionsList.layout and tree.layout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read header offsetHeight and update the virtual-row height during list layout
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per SessionsList.layout while the desktop header row exists
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The header was outside the virtual list; the removed customizations widget instead scanned its scroll DOM during desktop pane layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs on the resize/layout critical path, but the measured element is singular and updateElementHeight returns without re-render when its size is unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One transition per breakpoint change; resize frequency controls calls. Header cardinality is one, and visible list rows remain virtualized.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All DOM movement and layout run serially on the UI thread. There is no background concurrency or boundary fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates. The header element is reused rather than recreated, and virtual-list row templates are pooled by template ID.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added single geometry read, low that it is a net regression given the removed layout work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measurement quantifies the net resize cost, and the PR also removes prior customizations-pane scan/layout work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: resize adds one bounded header-height read while removing a larger customizations pane/layout path; evidence does not establish net degradation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Customizations active-state highlighting during editor navigation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: EditorService emits an active-editor change; one observable autorun on the rendered Customizations row toggles an active CSS class.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One constant-time instance check and class toggle per active-editor change while the row template is rendered.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous single-listener UI work; no queue, fan-out, or concurrent external operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: observableFromEvent subscribes only while observed by the row autorun and is owned by SessionsList, so disposal is bounded to the list lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the observable and renderer lifecycle.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Editor switching frequency varies, but work is constant and tiny.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression worth reporting: constant-time class updates are required for the new active indication and have bounded lifecycle.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 22 changed files and all diff pages. Traced desktop/phone list rendering, tree-splice behavior, resize/layout, editor opening, active-editor highlighting, harness synchronization, startup construction, disposal, and external-boundary cardinality. Submitted one medium-confidence-in-magnitude, high-confidence-in-mechanism synchronous-layout finding; no additional fan-out, retention, cache, concurrency, serialization, startup, or cleanup regression met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
